detail: Create, search, join and leave rooms modelled on sceNpMatching2. A search sees only the rooms of its own title, with each room's external data. Room messages, owner handoff when the owner leaves, and member pushes with each peer's address and P2P port.
note: Upstream work. Kick (`KICK_MEMBER`) is in the server but no test covers it.

detail: External and internal room data (only the owner writes it), room flags that searchers see (`SET_ROOM_DATA` which 2), and member data sent with `CREATE_ROOM` and `JOIN_ROOM` and returned in every member entry.
note: External and internal data are upstream work (0.1.0). Room flags and member data are newer, so clients built against 0.1.0 no longer match.

detail: An 8-character code per room (`SET_ROOM_ACCESS`, `JOIN_BY_CODE`, `GET_ROOM_ACCESS`). The room leaves search and the status page, which counts unlisted rooms. A connection that sends too many wrong codes is closed.
note: Protocol 0.4: `HELLO_ACK` flags bit 1 says the server has them. Codes are never logged.

detail: Matching2 room passwords, private slots and join by room ID. A relay-only variant that keeps members' addresses hidden from each other is also wanted.
note: Listed in ROADMAP.md under friends and invites; the relay-only variant is not in it yet.

detail: Modelled on sceNpScore: each player's best score is kept, a tie goes to whoever scored first, boards are higher-is-better or lower-is-better, and ranks are read by range or by online ID.
note: Upstream work. Kept in memory: a restart empties every board.

detail: Names are compared case-insensitively. A HELLO with a name held from another address gets ERROR 8 (name taken); from the same address it is the same player reconnecting, and the old connection is closed.
note: No passwords: a name is not authenticated.

detail: sceNpBasic: a friends list (everyone on the same server), presence (online, title, room), invites and join-a-friend, player history and a block list.
note: Not in the server today.

detail: Optional accounts next to the default of a name per player: sign-in through a generic OpenID Connect provider, or with Discord or GitHub.
note: Not started. The scope in ROADMAP.md says no accounts or passwords, so this needs that decision changed first.

detail: `-max-rooms`, `-max-player-rooms`, `-max-conns-per-addr`, `-max-req-rate` (requests per second per connection) and a size cap on room data. A request over a limit is refused; a connection over the rate is closed. Each refusal is logged at warn level.
evidence: server/limits_test.go, TestBlobLimit, TestPlayerRoomLimit, TestConnLimitPerAddr, TestRequestRateLimit, TestLogHelloAndRefusals
note: TCP only. UDP rate limits are planned (net-guardrails).

detail: `-log-level` (debug, info, warn, error), `-v` as debug, `-log-format` text or json, and `-log-file` to append to a file (mode 0600). Every refusal is logged at warn level; tokens and query strings are never logged.
note: Not checked: no test covers `-log-file`. The server does not rotate the file.

feature: Status page and /api/stats, with a token
detail: A read-only page and JSON on a separate listener, on localhost by default. `-http-token` requires a token (`Authorization: Bearer`, or `?token=`), and the server warns at start when the page is reachable from elsewhere without one.
note: The page and /api/stats are upstream work (0.1.0); the token is the fork's.

detail: `-trusted-proxies` (CIDRs or addresses) and `-proxy-protocol` (a PROXY v1 or v2 header required on the game TCP port from a listed proxy), and forwarded headers for the status page log. The real client address then counts for the limits, the name rule, `public_ip` and the log.
evidence: server/proxy.go, TestReadProxyHeader, TestClientAddr, TestProxyHeaderFromUntrustedPeerIsJunk, TestTrustedPeerWithoutHeaderIsClosed, TestLimitUsesRealAddress, #9, #12
note: Off by default. UDP is not proxied. See docs/running.md.

feature: Settings file, service unit and Traefik example
detail: `deploy/` holds `re-psn.env.example` (every setting, commented), a systemd unit and a Traefik config that sends PROXY v2. The release archives carry them as `examples/`.
note: `scripts/check-deploy.sh` checks the env file and the unit against the server's flags. The Traefik run (Traefik 3.1 under Podman) is recorded in docs/running.md; no run of the systemd unit is recorded.

detail: An nginx `stream` block with `proxy_protocol on;` (PROXY v1) and an HAProxy config with `send-proxy-v2`.
note: Not checked: neither config has been run against the server (docs/running.md says so).

detail: A Caddy config next to the other examples in `deploy/`.
note: Not started.

detail: A two-stage Dockerfile and a compose file in `docker/`, configured only by `RE_PSN_*` variables. The status page stays on localhost inside the container until a token is set.
note: A Podman 6.1 run is recorded in docker/README.md, and the NAT lab builds the image with Docker in CI. No image is published. Compose under Podman is not tested.

detail: Every flag can be set as `RE_PSN_<FLAG>`; the old `PSNR_<FLAG>` names still work as aliases. A flag wins, then `RE_PSN_`, then `PSNR_`. An old name logs a warning that names the variables, never the value. `-tcp-addr` and `-udp-addr` give the two game sockets their own addresses. A bad value stops the server at start.
evidence: server/config.go, TestEnvAlias, TestEnvNoticeHidesValue, TestFlagBeatsEnv, TestEnvBad, TestListenAddrs, #8, #17
note: No config file yet.

detail: A player's P2P socket sends the server a UDP PROBE. The server records the public endpoint and gives each viewer the address that works from where they are: the public one from another network, the LAN address from the same one.
note: Upstream work. The NAT lab runs it in Docker in CI.

detail: `-relay`, off by default: streams into a player behind a router go through the server, and datagrams go through the server's UDP port when punching does not get through (as with a symmetric NAT).
note: Upstream work. Uses the server's bandwidth; there is no per-player budget yet (net-guardrails).

detail: PROBE and RELAY packets are accepted only from the IP address of the player's TCP connection. A probe's `local_ip` is kept only if it is private, carrier-grade NAT, link-local or the probe's own source. `-udp-any-source` turns the check off.
note: A Podman run is recorded in docker/README.md.

detail: Per-source UDP rate limits and a failed-token counter, relay budgets (datagram size, per-player rates, idle streams), a 64-bit token, the limits written down, counters of dropped packets on /api/stats, and a test for each, with a fuzz test for the UDP packets.
note: Not started. The 64-bit token changes the wire format and waits for a protocol version bump.

detail: A check for players and hosts that says where a connection fails (server reachable, HELLO accepted, UDP probe answered, NAT behaviour, peer reachable, relay available) and shows round trip, loss and whether each peer is up.
note: Not designed yet.

detail: One file with no dependencies and no threads: `psnr_send` returns a request id, and `psnr_poll` hands out replies and pushes without blocking. It also builds the UDP probe and relay packets.
note: Upstream work. `TestCClient` skips without a C compiler; CI runs it on Linux only.

detail: A program for players and hosts: a terminal UI first, then a web UI served by the same binary, launch profiles per game, and a host mode.
note: Not started.

detail: Go fuzz targets for the frame parser, the request handlers and the PROXY header parser. Their seed inputs run with every `go test`.
note: CI runs the seeds only; longer fuzzing runs are by hand. The UDP packets have no fuzz target yet.

detail: gofmt, go vet, `go test -race` on Linux (with the C client) and `go test` on Windows, govulncheck, gitleaks over the full history, the NAT lab in Docker, and CodeQL for Go and the workflows. Actions are pinned and permissions are read-only by default.
note: Dependabot proposes version updates.

detail: Candidates: the C client outside Linux, the race detector on Windows, and a scan of the container image.
note: The list is not settled. The header of ci.yml says what CI does not check today.

detail: `scripts/release-build.sh` builds static binaries for windows/amd64, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 into `re-psn-vX.Y.Z-<os>-<arch>` archives with a .sha256 file each and SHA256SUMS. A pushed version tag makes a draft pre-release; a second workflow checks a published one.
note: Not released yet: there is no tag, so nothing has been published. The Windows and arm64 binaries are cross-built and not run.

detail: Written steps for cutting a release (tag, notes, checking the draft, publishing) and signed checksums.
note: Not written yet.
